findings: H1 commodity-markup SUPPORTED: haiku (~$0.037/trial) == fable@low (~$0.48/trial) outcomes on every shared cell; ~13x price gap for equal results.
H2 tier-ladder CHALLENGED: the axis is settled-vs-derived work, not difficulty. haiku 4.5 cleared T0-T4 hidden-graded 3/3 including the T4 semantic judge.
H3 uplift SUPPORTED: a cheap model lacks carried state and selection, not judgment; the harness supplies both (framing lifts it further).

principle: The settled-vs-derived line coincides with Clifford's candidate_only boundary. Retrieval is settled work with a deterministic validation surface AND has graph_effect none, so cheap models are both cost-optimal and epistemically safe there. The expensive residue is the one thing retrieval may not do by contract: promote a candidate to a finding.

haiku.role: settled/high-volume retrieval — almost all the token volume

sonnet.validation_surface: structured (join reconciles, order well-defined, threshold re-derivable)

invariant: No operation that promotes candidate->finding may run below the fable+human rung.
escalation: effort-first, evidence-driven (Tier-Bench escalate.py/rungs.py): start at the cheapest rung whose validation surface covers the op; escalate only on measured failure.
measurement: cost_per_success = average_cost / success_rate, per adapter per tier. Route on measured rows, not brand.
execution_note: Runs keyless via Claude Code subagents (Tier-Bench breadth runbook: cheap-prepares / top-adjudicates). Haiku/Sonnet subagents do acquisition + resolution; the top rung + human own promotion.
adapter_tier_default: haiku (retrieval); sonnet only where the adapter's job is resolution/join/screen.
